Axiom:
Before adding any dependency, verify four things: 1. **Node compatibility:** `npm view engines` — supports version in `.nvmrc`? 2. **Module system compatibility:** package ESM-only / CJS-only / dual? Matches project's `"type"`? 3. **Pinning discipline:** dev tool → `--save-exact`; runtime dep → range acceptable. 4. **Release channel:** the `latest` dist-tag is not guaranteed stable — it can point at a pre-release (`rc` / `beta` / `alpha`). Before pinning, compare `npm view version` (what `latest` actually resolves to) against `npm view dist-tags` (the full tag → version map) and pin the newest version that reads as stable (no `-rc`/`-beta`/`-alpha` suffix), not whatever `latest` happens to name at that moment. Installing a pre-release is permitted only as an explicit, spec-recorded decision — never a side effect of trusting `latest` by default.
Skipping these introduces incompatibilities that surface as cryptic runtime errors, not install errors.
